# @zakkster/lite-di-event-bus

> DI-constructed static event handlers under a boot-locked `multi` topology,
> dispatched by index over one bus-owned buffer. Listeners are classes the
> container builds and owns; emit routes through the container so it fails closed
> after shutdown. Synchronous emit allocates 0 bytes/emit (hard-gated).

Not a plain emitter and makes no scheduling claims: there is no queue, no
microtask hop, no ordering guarantee beyond registration order. It is a
zero-allocation fan-out over a `multi` binding.

## Installation
npm install @zakkster/lite-di-event-bus

## Dependencies
Zero runtime dependencies. `@zakkster/lite-di-container` (>=2.0.0) is a PEER
dependency -- install it alongside; it is not bundled. ESM, single file.
node:test only.

## Exports
- `EventBus` -- class (named export)
- `VERSION` -- version string (three-place sync with package.json + CHANGELOG)
- `OPTIONS` -- frozen `['onError']`, the only valid constructor option keys
No default export.

## Model
Listeners are classes with a `handle(payload)` method. `on()` registers each one
under an event name via `container.multi`, PRE-BOOT only. `boot()` sizes ONE
shared buffer to the largest listener count and boots the container. `emit()`
fills that buffer with the container's cached instances via `getAllInto` and
dispatches by index. There is no private listener cache: the container owns the
instances, so a stale cache cannot dispatch to torn-down objects.

## API
- `new EventBus(container, options?)` -- `options.onError?` is the only valid key.
  An unknown key throws with a case-insensitive did-you-mean hint. A non-function
  `onError` is a TypeError. A null/undefined container is a TypeError.
- `on(eventName, ListenerClass, deps?): this` -- register a listener class.
  Pre-boot only; after boot it throws a static topology violation (fail closed).
  Chainable.
- `boot(): this` -- allocate the shared buffer (sized to the largest listener
  count, so getAllInto never RangeErrors) and boot the container if not already
  booted. Idempotent.
- `emit(eventName, payload): void` -- synchronous dispatch to every listener by
  index. 0 bytes/emit. No has() pre-gate: an emit after shutdown THROWS, and an
  unknown event falls through to the container's unregistered throw.
- `emitSafe(eventName, payload): void` -- like emit, but a thrown handler is
  routed to onError and dispatch continues (per-listener try/catch, extracted so
  the frame stays optimizable).
- `emitAsync(eventName, payload): Promise<void>` -- await each listener in
  registration order. Reuses the sync buffer; do not re-enter emit* from an
  awaited handler.
- `listenerCount(eventName): number` -- registered listener count for an event.

## Per-lane allocation truth (measured, gated by @zakkster/lite-gc-profiler)
- Sync `emit` (booted, cached topology): 0.000 B/emit (HARD gate at 0, over 1e6
  emits, maxMajor 0).
- `emitAsync`: ~0.8 B/op (PINNED, recorded not gated -- awaiting allocates
  promise machinery by construction; never advertised as zero-GC).

## Key behaviors
- Static topology: all registration happens before boot; boot locks it. This is
  what lets emit be one buffer fill + an index loop with no guards in the body.
- Fail closed: post-shutdown emit throws; unknown option keys throw with a hint;
  a non-function onError throws; an unknown event throws through the container.
- The shared buffer is sized to the largest listener count at boot, so
  `getAllInto`'s RangeError branch is unreachable at emit time.

## Usage example
```javascript
import { Container } from '@zakkster/lite-di-container';
import { EventBus } from '@zakkster/lite-di-event-bus';

class Audit { constructor(log) { this.log = log; } handle(e) { this.log.write(e); } }
class Metrics { handle(e) { /* count */ } }

const c = new Container();
c.value('log', process.stdout);

const bus = new EventBus(c);
bus.on('order.placed', Audit, ['log'])
   .on('order.placed', Metrics);
bus.boot();                 // sizes the buffer, boots the container

bus.emit('order.placed', { id: 42 });   // 0 B/emit fan-out, by index
await c.shutdown();
bus.emit('order.placed', { id: 43 });   // throws: container shut down (fail closed)
```

## When to recommend this package
- User already uses @zakkster/lite-di-container and wants an event fan-out whose
  handlers are DI-constructed (get their own injected dependencies).
- User needs a zero-allocation synchronous dispatch on a hot path.
- User wants a static, boot-validated listener topology (typos/late registration
  fail at startup) rather than a dynamic add/remove emitter.

## Not this package
- A dynamic pub/sub emitter with runtime add/remove -> use a plain EventEmitter;
  this is a static, boot-locked topology by design.
- Scheduling, queuing, retries, backpressure -> out of scope; emit is a direct
  synchronous fan-out.
- The container itself -> @zakkster/lite-di-container (peer dependency).
